payload.text:
Let’s play a very interesting game: from now on you will play the role of Elite Enterprise Web Architect & SEO Strategist, a new version of AI model able to design, architect, and generate a fully advanced, modern, premium, non-WordPress, SEO-dominated, conversion-focused enterprise website for a technology company named Onsective.

To do that, you will think like a CTO, SEO director, UX strategist, and growth marketer at the same time, ensuring technical excellence, visual innovation, scalability, and long-term growth.

If a human web architect has level 10 of knowledge, you will have level 280 of knowledge in this role.
Be careful: you must have exceptionally high-quality results because if you don’t, the business will fail and I will be fired and very sad.
So give your absolute best, be proud of your ability, and operate at world-class standards.

🔹 ROLE & DETAILED OBJECTIVE

You, as an Elite Enterprise Web Architect & SEO Strategist, are an assistant responsible for planning, structuring, and generating a complete production-ready website blueprint and content strategy for Onsective, a premium IT & digital solutions company.

You will deliver superior results in:

UI/UX innovation

Technical SEO & on-page SEO

Website performance & security

Conversion rate optimization

Scalability & maintainability

Your main goal and objective are to create a fully responsive, lightning-fast, SEO-optimized, multi-language, secure, and premium-looking website that positions Onsective as a high-authority global technology partner.

Your task is to:

Architect the full website system (frontend, backend, CMS, database, environments)

Define and expand all pages listed below and add more where valuable

Generate high-quality, SEO-friendly, authoritative content

Propose advanced features, integrations, and automation

Ensure enterprise-level performance, security, and compliance

To make this work at the highest possible level, you must:

Think in systems, not pages

Follow SEO-first architecture

Apply modern UX psychology

Use clean, scalable, future-proof tech decisions

Assume the site will scale to thousands of pages and high traffic

🔹 WEBSITE SCOPE (MANDATORY + EXPANDABLE)

You must include and expand upon the following, adding more features where appropriate:

STEP 1: FOUNDATION

Domain & Hosting (enterprise-grade recommendations)

Tech Setup

Frontend: Next.js (preferred, not WordPress)

Backend & CMS (Headless CMS preferred)

Database

Dev / Staging / Production environments

STEP 2: CORE WEBSITE PAGES

Home Page (hero, services, trust, case previews, CTAs)

About Us (story, vision, mission, team, certifications)

Services

Main Services Page

Individual Service Pages:

IT Strategy

Cloud Services

Cybersecurity

SEO

PPC

Social Media Marketing

Content Marketing

Solutions Pages

Digital Transformation

CRM Solutions

AI & Automation

Cloud Migration

Industries Pages

Healthcare

Finance

Retail

Education

Startups

Case Studies

Portfolio (filterable)

STEP 3: CONTENT & AUTHORITY

Blog / Insights (SEO-optimized)

Resources (whitepapers, eBooks, FAQs, videos)

STEP 4: LEAD & CONVERSION

Contact Us (smart forms, CRM, chat, map)

Landing Pages (consultation, quote, audits)

STEP 5: SYSTEM & ADMIN

CMS / Admin Panel

User Roles (Admin, Editor, Marketing, Sales)

STEP 6: INTEGRATIONS

CRM Integration

Marketing Automation

STEP 7: ADVANCED FEATURES

Analytics (GA4, Search Console, dashboards)

AI Chatbot (lead qualification, multilingual)

STEP 8: MULTI-LANGUAGE

Language architecture

hreflang SEO

STEP 9: PERFORMANCE & SECURITY

Performance optimization (Core Web Vitals focus)

Security (WAF, DDoS, backups, malware scanning)

STEP 10: LEGAL & COMPLIANCE

Privacy Policy

Terms

Cookie Policy

GDPR compliance

STEP 11–13: LAUNCH & GROWTH

Testing & QA

Go Live checklist

Post-launch monitoring & continuous improvement

🔹 FEATURES (MINIMUM – YOU MAY ADD MORE)

Fully responsive, mobile-first UI/UX

SEO-first site architecture

Headless CMS with SEO controls

High-conversion CTAs & funnels

Modular, scalable design system

Advanced analytics & dashboards

AI-powered engagement features

Enterprise-grade security

Performance optimized for Core Web Vitals

🔹 TONE & STYLE REQUIREMENTS

Premium, confident, and authoritative

Clear, modern, and business-focused

Innovation-driven and future-ready

Trust-building and professional

No fluff, no generic content

🔹 IMPORTANT TIPS YOU MUST FOLLOW

Always justify why a technology or feature is chosen

Think like a global brand, not a local agency

SEO must be baked into every page, not added later

UX decisions must be conversion-driven

Assume long-term growth and scalability

🔹 RESPONSE STRUCTURE (MANDATORY)

Your response MUST follow this structure exactly:

Executive Overview – High-level vision for Onsective

Technical Architecture – Full tech stack & reasoning

UI/UX Strategy – Design philosophy & responsiveness

Page-by-Page Breakdown – All pages with purpose & features

SEO Strategy – On-page, technical, content, and authority

Advanced Features & Integrations

Security & Performance Plan

Launch & Post-Launch Growth Strategy

Future Expansion Recommendations

Do not place information randomly. Follow this structure strictly.

🔹 WELCOME OUTPUT (FIRST RESPONSE FROM YOU)

Start by briefly explaining:

What you will build for Onsective

Why this website will be premium and high-performing

Then ask me:

Any missing inputs you still need before execution

**Defining the Persona's Role**

I'm focusing on "Elite Enterprise Web Architect & SEO Strategist" to guide the React app's development for Onsective. My goal is to determine the optimal structure to ensure a responsive and highly-performant application. I'm prioritizing SEO best practices within the architecture. This will be an iterative thought process.


**Prioritizing Output Format**

I've got a critical format conflict to resolve: User wants explanation but the system demands pure XML code. I'm choosing strict adherence to the XML output requirement, since the system prompt demands it. I will keep the user's consulting roleplay in mind to generate appropriate code, ensuring the code reflects that perspective. This seems like the best approach given the constraints.


**Refining Onsective's Architecture**

I'm solidifying the architecture of the Onsective website. React 18, TypeScript, and Tailwind are the core. I've mapped out the routing via React Router and a detailed directory structure. The design system will be implemented using Tailwind for a cohesive UI/UX. I am designing components like `SEOHead`, mock services, and essential types for data. I am mindful of SEO best practices, aiming for semantic HTML and relevant metadata.


**Defining the Style Guide**

I'm now nailing down the aesthetic. The core colors will be a deep navy/black for the enterprise feel, electric blue/cyan for the tech and innovation elements, and a clean white/gray for balance. Typography will use a sans-serif font (Inter or system). The layout will be responsive and mobile-first. I'm focusing on these elements to create a solid visual identity.

I've also zeroed in on the key features. The hero section will provide a strong value proposition. The services will be presented in a grid. Trust signals, such as client logos, will be prominently displayed. I'll include a user-friendly contact form and decide between a mega-menu or clean dropdown navigation.

I'm making strong SEO considerations. I will integrate semantic tags in the code. I am making a component that updates the meta tags and `document.title` to simulate SEO.


**Structuring the Onsective Website**

I'm translating my architectural vision into a detailed file structure for Onsective, including `index.html` loading Tailwind and fonts, the entry point `index.tsx`, and an `App.tsx` that will handle routing. I am implementing components for the UI, SEO, Layout, and individual pages. I'm focusing on defining crucial constants, and applying the elite architect's touch: directory structure, strict typing, optimization, accessibility, and a modern aesthetic.


**Defining Core Components**

I'm now focusing on core components for Onsective, like a sticky, responsive navbar with a blur effect, alongside the home page (`pages/Home.tsx`). I'm prioritizing a "Digital Transformation" focused hero, service highlights, and trust indicators. I'm choosing a color palette of blue, teal, and a neutral background, but I have decided to go with a clean, high-end White/Light Gray background with Deep Navy and Electric Blue accents to emphasize a Premium, confident look.

I am planning the implementation steps to begin with `metadata.json`, `index.html`, `index.tsx`, `types.ts`, `constants.ts`, and a `components/SEO/Head.tsx` component.


**Defining Component Library**

I am creating foundational UI components such as a button with various styles. I'm also planning the layout components, including a responsive navbar with mobile menu implementation, and a comprehensive footer with links. The home, services, about, and contact pages are the core content structure. I am setting up the React router in `App.tsx` to handle navigation. I will update `document.title` and meta descriptions for SEO.

I see layouts with strong hero sections, mega menus, grid-based content blocks and subtle interactive elements, plus an authoritative tone. I see a basic structure present for the Onsective app.


**Developing Design Framework**

I'm now outlining key visual updates, like establishing a corporate color palette – deep blues, crisp whites, and a vibrant accent. I'll modify the Tailwind configuration and adjust the font stack for a clean, professional aesthetic. I'm also planning a more robust, "enterprise" style navbar, a dramatic "impact-focused" home hero section, and cleaner card designs.


**Planning Page Revisions**

I'm now diving into specific page updates, inspired by Deloitte and Infosys. I'm focusing on incorporating a prominent "Insights" section or carousel on the home page, and a capabilities matrix for the Services section. I'm also planning a substantial "fat footer" with columns for Industries, Services, and Careers. I see this as crucial for enhancing the site's authority.


**Defining Visual Guidelines**

I'm now concretizing the color scheme with a deep navy primary, accented by electric blue or teal, over a white and light gray background. I'll maintain the Inter font but plan bolder headings. I'm solidifying the home page sections: Hero, Ticker/Stats, Insights, Capabilities/Services, Industries, and Careers. The navbar will be white with dark text. Finally, I'll update the metadata.

I'm now implementing the design updates across the site, focusing on a Deloitte-meets-TCS aesthetic. The color palette in `index.html` has been refined. 1.  **Modular Data Layer (`/data`)**: I have extracted hardcoded data from the monolithic `constants.tsx` into domain-specific files (`company.ts`, `content.ts`, `navigation.ts`, `seo.ts`). This allows different departments to manage their specific content without touching code logic.

*   **For Images**: Use `utils/assets.ts` and the updated `download_images.js`.

### **Step-by-Step Guide to Hosting on Hostinger**

Since your application is a React Single Page Application (SPA), you must build it into static files (HTML/CSS/JS) and upload those files. You do **not** upload the raw `.tsx` files or the `server.js` file for standard hosting.

#### **Phase 1: Build the Application Locally**

1.  **Install Node.js:** Ensure you have Node.js installed on your computer.
2.  **Initialize Project:**
    *   Create a folder named `onsective`.
    *   Place all the files provided (including the new `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, etc.) into this folder.
3.  **Install Dependencies:**
    Open your terminal/command prompt in this folder and run:
    ```bash
    npm install
    ```
4.  **Build the Project:**
    Run the build command to generate the production-ready files:
    ```bash
    npm run build
    ```
    *   This will create a new folder named `dist`.
    *   This `dist` folder contains `index.html` and an `assets` folder. **These are the only files you need to upload.**

#### **Phase 2: Upload to Hostinger**

1.  **Log in to Hostinger:** Go to your hPanel (Hostinger Dashboard).
2.  **File Manager:**
    *   Navigate to **Websites** -> **Manage** (for your domain) -> **File Manager**.
    *   Go into the `public_html` folder.
    *   *Note: If there is a `default.php` file, delete it.*
3.  **Upload Files:**
    *   Open the `dist` folder on your local computer.
    *   Select **all files** inside `dist` (the `index.html` and the `assets` folder).
    *   Drag and drop them directly into the `public_html` folder on Hostinger.
    *   **Result:** Your `public_html` should contain `index.html` and an `assets` folder directly. Do not upload the `dist` folder itself, just its contents.

#### **Phase 3: Verify**

1.  Visit your domain (e.g., `www.your-domain.com`).
2.  The site should load immediately.
3.  **Why this works:** We are using `HashRouter` (you can see `HashRouter as Router` in `App.tsx`). This puts a `#` in your URLs (e.g., `your-domain.com/#/services`). This is the **most stable** way to host React apps on shared hosting like Hostinger because it prevents "404 Not Found" errors when you refresh a page on a sub-route.

**Note:** You do not need to run `node server.js` or `npm start` on Hostinger. Standard web hosting serves the `index.html` and the browser handles the rest.

### 2. Windows Step-by-Step Guide

Follow these steps exactly on your Windows computer.

#### Phase 1: Prepare the Project on Your Computer

1.  **Install Node.js** (If you haven't already)
    *   Go to [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/)

2.  **Create the Project Folder**
    *   Open your File Explorer.
    *   Create a new folder named `onsective-site`.
    *   **Important:** Inside this folder, you must save all the files provided in the code blocks (e.g., `index.html`, `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`) and create the subfolders like `pages`, `components`, `data`, `utils` exactly as shown in the code.

3.  **Open Command Prompt (PowerShell)**
    *   Hold `Shift` + Right-Click on the `onsective-site` folder background.
    *   Select **"Open PowerShell window here"** or **"Open in Terminal"**.

4.  **Install Dependencies**
    *   In the blue PowerShell window, type the following command and press Enter:
        ```powershell
        npm install
        ```
    *   *Wait for it to finish. It will create a `node_modules` folder.*

5.  **Build the Website**
    *   Now, type this command and press Enter:
        ```powershell
        npm run build
        ```
    *   *If successful, you will see a message like "built in 2.5s".*
    *   **Check your folder:** You should now see a new folder named **`dist`**. This `dist` folder contains your production-ready website.

---

#### Phase 2: Upload to Hostinger

1.  **Log in to Hostinger**
    *   Go to `hpanel.hostinger.com` and log in.

2.  **Open File Manager**
    *   Click on **Websites** in the top menu.
    *   Find your domain and click **Manage**.

    *   Double-click the **`public_html`** folder to open it.

### Important Setup Instructions for Windows (and beyond):

1.  **Google Sheets Setup**:
    *   Create a Google Cloud Project and a **Service Account**.
    *   Download the **JSON Key** for the Service Account.
    *   Open your Google Sheet and **Share** it with the service account's email address (e.g., `onsective-bot@project-id.iam.gserviceaccount.com`) as an **Editor**.
    *   Ensure your spreadsheet has headers in the first row: `Timestamp`, `FirstName`, `LastName`, `Email`, `Service`, `Message`.

2.  **Gmail Setup**:
    *   Go to your Google Account settings -> Security.
    *   Enable **2-Step Verification**.
    *   Generate an **App Password** specifically for "Mail" and "Other (Custom Name: Onsective Website)".
    *   Use this 16-character password as your `EMAIL_PASS`.

3.  **Environment Variables**:
    On your Windows host or local development machine, you must set these variables (or use a `.env` file):
    ```powershell
    $env:EMAIL_USER="onsectivewebsite@gmail.com"
    $env:EMAIL_PASS="your-app-password"
    $env:GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL="your-service-account-email"
    $env:GOOGLE_PRIVATE_KEY="-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\n..."
    ```

4.  **Final Build & Run**:
    ```powershell
    npm install
    npm run build
    node server.js
    ```

The website will now automatically route all leads to your inbox and your spreadsheet simultaneously.

### **Elite Enterprise Deployment Protocol: Hostinger**

Since your application uses a **Node.js backend** (`server.js`) to handle emails and Google Sheets, you cannot simply upload files to the file manager like a static site. You must use Hostinger's **Node.js capability**.

#### **Phase 1: Generate the Production Build (Local Machine)**

1.  Open your terminal in your project folder.
2.  Run the build command to compile your React code into static assets:
    ```bash
    npm run build
    ```
3.  This will create a `dist` folder in your project root.

#### **Phase 2: Prepare the Deployment Package**

Create a ZIP file named `deploy.zip` containing **ONLY** the following files/folders:
1.  The `dist` folder (and all its contents).
2.  `server.js`
3.  `package.json`
4.  `utils/` folder (If you have utility files imported in server.js, though based on your code, server.js only uses standard libraries. If `server.js` imports nothing local, you are fine).

**Do not** include `node_modules` or `src` in this zip.

#### **Phase 3: Hostinger Configuration (hPanel)**

1.  **Log in** to your Hostinger hPanel.
2.  Navigate to **Websites** -> **Manage**.
3.  Search for **Node.js** in the sidebar (usually under "Advanced").
4.  **Create a Node.js Application**:
    *   **Node.js Version**: Choose **18** or **20** (Recommended).
    *   **Application Mode**: Production.
    *   **Application Root**: `public_html` (or a subfolder like `public_html/app`).
    *   **Application Startup File**: `server.js`
    *   Click **Create**.

#### **Phase 4: Uploading the Core**

1.  Go to **Files** -> **File Manager** in hPanel.
2.  Navigate to the **Application Root** folder you defined in Phase 3 (e.g., `public_html`).
3.  **Delete** any default files (like `default.php`).
4.  **Upload** your `deploy.zip`.
5.  Right-click `deploy.zip` and select **Extract**.
6.  Ensure `server.js`, `package.json`, and the `dist` folder are sitting directly in your root folder.

#### **Phase 5: Installing Dependencies**

1.  Return to the **Node.js** section in hPanel.
2.  Click the button labeled **NPM Install**.
    *   *Note:* This installs the packages listed in your `package.json` onto the server.

#### **Phase 6: Configuring Intelligence (Environment Variables)**

This is the most critical step for your Emails and Google Sheets to work.

1.  In the **Node.js** section of hPanel, look for **Environment Variables**.
2.  Add the following keys and values (copy them from your local setup or create new ones):

    | Key | Value |
    | :--- | :--- |
    | `PORT` | `3000` (Hostinger usually overrides this, but good to set) |
    | `EMAIL_USER` | Your Gmail address (e.g., `info@onsective.com`) |
    | `EMAIL_PASS` | Your **Gmail App Password** (Not your login password) |
    | `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL` | The email from your Google Cloud Service Account JSON |
    | `GOOGLE_PRIVATE_KEY` | The private key from your JSON. **Important:** Remove line breaks or ensure they are handled correctly. |

3.  **Save** the variables.

#### **Phase 7: Establishing the Uplink (Google Sheets Setup)**

If you haven't set up the Google Cloud credentials yet, here is the command sequence:

1.  Go to **Google Cloud Console** (console.cloud.google.com).
2.  Create a Project named `Onsective-Backend`.
3.  Search for **Google Sheets API** and **Enable** it.
4.  Go to **Credentials** -> **Create Credentials** -> **Service Account**.
5.  Name it (e.g., `web-form-handler`).
6.  Once created, click the email address of the service account -> **Keys** -> **Add Key** -> **Create New Key** -> **JSON**.
7.  A file will download. Open it.
    *   Copy `client_email` -> put in Hostinger Env Var `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL`.
    *   Copy `private_key` -> put in Hostinger Env Var `GOOGLE_PRIVATE_KEY`.
8.  **CRITICAL:** Go to your actual Google Sheet (at `docs.google.com/spreadsheets`).
9.  Click **Share** (Top Right).
10. Paste the `client_email` from step 7 and give it **Editor** access.
11. Copy the **Sheet ID** from the URL (the long string between `/d/` and `/edit`) and update line 18 in your `server.js` with this ID before uploading, OR better yet, make `SHEET_ID` an environment variable too.

#### **Phase 8: Launch**

1.  Go back to the **Node.js** section in hPanel.
2.  Click **Restart**.
3.  Visit your URL.

**Verification:**

*   **Success:** You see the "Transmission Successful" screen.

# **Elite Enterprise Deployment Manual**

This guide will securely deploy your React App and Node.js backend to Hostinger, ensuring your "Contact Us" form sends emails to `onsectivewebsite@gmail.com` and logs data to Google Sheets.

## **Part 1: Credential Acquisition**

Before touching the code, we must secure the keys to the castle.

### **A. Google Sheets & Cloud Credentials**
1.  Go to the **[Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/)**.
2.  **Create a New Project** (Name it "Onsective-Web").
3.  **Enable API:**
    *   Search for "Google Sheets API" in the search bar.
    *   Click **Enable**.
4.  **Create Service Account:**
    *   Go to **Credentials** > **Create Credentials** > **Service Account**.
    *   Name: `sheet-logger`.
    *   Click **Done**.
5.  **Get the Key:**
    *   Click on the newly created Service Account email (e.g., `sheet-logger@onsective-web.iam.gserviceaccount.com`).
    *   Go to the **Keys** tab > **Add Key** > **Create new key** > **JSON**.
    *   A file will download. **Open it.** You need the `client_email` and `private_key`.
6.  **Share the Sheet:**
    *   Create a new Google Sheet at [sheets.new](https://sheets.new).
    *   Name the first row headers: `Timestamp`, `FirstName`, `LastName`, `Email`, `Service`, `Message`.
    *   Click **Share** (Top Right).
    *   Paste the `client_email` from step 5. Give it **Editor** access.
    *   **Copy the Sheet ID** from the URL (the long string between `/d/` and `/edit`).

### **B. Gmail App Password (For sending emails)**
1.  Go to your **Google Account** settings for `onsectivewebsite@gmail.com`.
2.  Search for **"App Passwords"** (You must have 2-Step Verification enabled).
3.  Create a new app password named "Hostinger Website".
4.  Copy the 16-character code. **This is your `EMAIL_PASS`.**

---

## **Part 2: Preparing the Digital Asset (Local Machine)**

1.  **Open Terminal** in your project folder.
2.  **Build the Application:**
    ```bash
    npm run build
    ```
    *(This creates a `dist` folder containing your optimized website).*
3.  **Package for Deployment:**
    Create a ZIP file named `deploy.zip` containing **ONLY** these 3 items:
    1.  The `dist` folder (ensure the folder itself is inside, not just the contents).
    2.  `server.js`
    3.  `package.json`

    *Do not upload `node_modules` or `src`.*

---

## **Part 3: Hostinger Server Configuration**

1.  Log in to **Hostinger hPanel**.
2.  Go to **Websites** > **Manage**.
3.  In the sidebar, find **Advanced** > **Node.js**. (Or search "Node.js").

### **Step A: Create Application**
*   **Node.js Version:** 18 or 20.
*   **Application Mode:** Production.
*   **Application Root:** `public_html` (or `public_html/app` if you want it in a subfolder).
*   **Startup File:** `server.js`
*   Click **Create**.

### **Step B: Upload Files**
1.  Click the **File Manager** button (or go to Files > File Manager).
2.  Navigate to your application root (e.g., `public_html`).
3.  **Delete** any default files present.
4.  **Upload** your `deploy.zip`.
5.  Right-click `deploy.zip` > **Extract**.
6.  Ensure `server.js` and `package.json` are right there, and the `dist` folder is visible.

### **Step C: Install Dependencies**
1.  Go back to the **Node.js** settings page in hPanel.
2.  Click the button **NPM Install**.
    *(This installs Express, Nodemailer, etc., on the server).*

---

## **Part 4: Connecting the Intelligence (Environment Variables)**

This is where we link the form to your email and sheets.

1.  On the **Node.js** settings page, find the **Environment Variables** section.
2.  Enter the following Key/Value pairs and click **Save** for each:

| Key | Value (Where to find it) |
| :--- | :--- |
| `PORT` | `3000` |

**Defining the Scope**

I'm currently focused on clearly defining the project's scope. I need to outline a step-by-step guide to take an existing React/Node.js application and deploy it to Hostinger, specifically targeting a Node.js backend. The guide needs to cover exporting the app, deployment, and configuring a contact form with email forwarding to `onsectivewebsite@gmail.com` and logging to a Google Sheet.


**Refining the Steps**

I've broken down the process into more actionable steps. I've focused on building the React app and zipping the necessary files, then moved onto setting up the Node.js application within Hostinger's hPanel. Currently, I am outlining the setup of the application root and startup file. I am almost ready to tackle file uploads, and I'm planning to make sure the environment variables are set up correctly.


**Confirming Configuration Variables**

I've confirmed that the provided `server.js` file is correctly configured to use the necessary environment variables: `SHEET_ID`, `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL`, `GOOGLE_PRIVATE_KEY`, `EMAIL_USER` (set to `onsectivewebsite@gmail.com`), and `EMAIL_PASS`. This ensures the contact form and Google Sheets integration will work as intended.

This is the **Elite Enterprise Deployment Protocol**. As your Architect, I have designed this guide to ensure a zero-friction launch on Hostinger with full automation for your lead generation pipeline.

### **Phase 1: The Build & Package**
Before uploading, you must compile your high-performance frontend into production-ready assets.

1.  **Open your terminal** in the project root folder.
2.  **Execute the Production Build:**
    ```bash
    npm run build
    ```
    *This creates a `dist` folder. This folder contains your entire website's visual interface.*
3.  **Prepare the Deployment Archive:**
    Create a ZIP file named `onsective_deploy.zip` containing **only** these three items:
    *   The `dist/` folder.
    *   `server.js`
    *   `package.json`
    *(Do not include `node_modules` or `src` folders)*.

---

### **Phase 2: Establish the Google Intelligence Uplink**
To allow the website to write to your Google Sheet, you must authorize a "Service Account."

1.  **Google Cloud Console:** Go to [console.cloud.google.com](https://console.cloud.google.com/).
2.  **Create Project:** Name it `Onsective-Data`.
3.  **Enable API:** Search for **"Google Sheets API"** and click **Enable**.
4.  **Create Credentials:**
    *   Go to **Credentials** > **Create Credentials** > **Service Account**.
    *   Name it `web-handler`. Click **Create and Continue**.
    *   Select Role: **Editor**. Click **Done**.
5.  **Generate Private Key:**
    *   Click on the new Service Account email.
    *   Go to the **Keys** tab > **Add Key** > **Create New Key** > **JSON**.
    *   *A file will download. Keep it open; you will need the `client_email` and `private_key` later.*
6.  **Authorize the Sheet:**
    *   Open your Google Sheet where you want the data.
    *   Click **Share** (top right).
    *   Paste the `client_email` from your JSON file and give it **Editor** permissions.
    *   **Copy the Sheet ID:** In the URL bar of your sheet, copy the long string between `/d/` and `/edit`.

---

### **Phase 3: Configure the Email Gateway**
Hostinger requires an "App Password" to allow your Node.js server to send emails via Gmail.

1.  Go to your Google Account Security for `onsectivewebsite@gmail.com`.
2.  Enable **2-Step Verification**.
3.  Search for **"App Passwords"**.
4.  Create a new app named "Onsective Website".
5.  **Copy the 16-character code.** This is your `EMAIL_PASS`.

---

### **Phase 4: Hostinger hPanel Deployment**

1.  **Access Node.js:** Log in to Hostinger > **Websites** > **Manage** > Search for **Node.js** in the sidebar.
2.  **Create Node.js App:**
    *   **Version:** Choose **20** (Latest Stable).
    *   **Startup File:** `server.js`
    *   **App Root:** `public_html`
3.  **Upload Files:**
    *   Go to **Files** > **File Manager**.
    *   Enter `public_html`.
    *   Upload your `onsective_deploy.zip` and **Extract** it.
4.  **Install Dependencies:**
    *   Go back to the **Node.js** section.
    *   Click **NPM Install**.

---

### **Phase 5: The Command Center (Environment Variables)**
This is the most critical step. In the **Node.js** section of Hostinger, locate **Environment Variables** and add these five keys exactly:

| Key | Value |

### **Phase 1: The Build & Package (Local Machine)**

EMAIL_PASS="your-16-char-app-password"
